thread.title: Gold set to post back-to-back gains as stocks extend wobbly start to the year - MarketWatch

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Gold set to post back-to-back gains as stocks extend wobbly start to the year - MarketWatch
text:
Gold futures on Thursday extended a climb toward its highest level in more than six months as U.S. stocks staged a sharp pullback and the dollar softened.
“Obviously, the concerning news from Apple sales in China has created an additional wave of equity market selling, and that in turn has continued to pump money towards gold,” analysts at Zaner Precious Metals wrote in a daily report.
A bearish revenue outlook from iPhone-maker Apple Inc. AAPL, -8.43% rattled markets , with investors pushing the technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -1.88% sharply lower. 2.35% and the S&P 500 index SPX, -1.75% also declined.
Apple shares headed lower after the tech giant announced a rare cut to its sales forecast , citing sluggish economic growth in China, which could also be exacerbated by the longstanding tariff dispute between Beijing and Washington.
Apple’s late-Wednesday announcement has provided further evidence that the world’s second largest economy is on an uneven footing, which could deliver fresh worries of contraction in international economic expansion, market participants said.
February gold on Comex GCG9, +0.54% gained $7.70, or 0.6%, to $1,291.80 an ounce, after the commodity closed 0.2% higher in the prior session . Prices look set to mark another finish at its highest since the middle of June, according to FactSet data.
Equity market jitters to start 2019 and growing expectations of a pause in coming rate increases by the Federal Reserve, which has become more cognizant of the market’s tailspin lower , has helped support bullion prices.
“After months of indecision, gold appears to be in a clearly defined uptrend. Yes, it’s overbought, but it has been that way for week,” wrote Stephen Todd, editor and publisher of financial blog Todd Market Forecast, in a Thursday report.
Supporting gains for gold was a softer dollar, with a measure of the buck, the ICE U.S. Dollar DXY, -0.35% off 0.5% at 96.35.
Meanwhile, silver, a precious metal that tends to be more sensitive to signs of global economic weakness, punched higher after healthy private-sector employment data from ADP.
March silver SIH9, +0.39% was picking up 5.1 cents, or 0.3%, to reach $15.71, after trading lower earlier Thursday. Silver closed up 0.7% on Wednesday.
Automatic Data Processing Inc. ADP, -2.22% showed that 271,000 private-sector jobs were added in December, compared with a previous monthly reading of 179,000.
Market participants are awaiting the more closely followed nonfarm-payroll report on Friday, with 184,000 jobs expected in December and an unemployment rate at 3.6%.
“With gold diverging with the rest of the precious metals complex it is clear it remains the sole flight to quality instrument, with silver, platinum and palladium faltering under the fear of softer physical demand in the event that the Chinese economy slows precipitously,” analysts at Zaner Precious metals said.
On Comex, April platinum PLJ9, -0.37% traded at $797.60 an ounce, down 0.8%, w hile March palladium PAH9, -0.13% shed 0.2% to $1,196.50 an ounce. March copper HGH9, -2.63% fell by 2% to $2.57 a pound.

Among the exchange-traded funds, SPDR Gold Shares GLD, +0.51% added 0.6% and the VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF GDX, +0.64% rose 0.8%.
